vocabulary.meaning_en: a little sad, often for no clear reason
vocabulary.example: I feel a bit down today.
She's been feeling blue all week.
I've had a cold for two weeks and I feel miserable.
The children were distraught when the cat disappeared.
He was gutted when he didn't get the job.
We were devastated by the news.

vocabulary.meaning_en: very lonely and sad; (a place) empty and sad
vocabulary.example: It was a desolate island with nobody living on it.

vocabulary.meaning_en: so sad that nobody can comfort you
vocabulary.example: After the final, Tommy was inconsolable.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (person) very sad after a terrible event
vocabulary.example: After losing his business, he was a broken man.

vocabulary.word: at the end of your tether
vocabulary.meaning_en: so tired or upset that you can't take any more
vocabulary.meaning_ar: نفد صبره / وصل إلى أقصى احتماله
vocabulary.note_ar: ويقال أيضًا at the end of your rope
vocabulary.note_en: Also: at the end of your rope.
vocabulary.example: With all this pressure, I'm at the end of my tether.

vocabulary.meaning_en: (UK, informal, humorous) very disappointed, often about football
vocabulary.example: His team lost the final. He's as sick as a parrot.
I tried to console him, but he kept crying.
I feel down, but I can't put my finger on why.

fine_lines.title: From a little sad to extremely sad
fine_lines.explanation_ar: down وblue = حزن خفيف. miserable وgutted = حزن أو خيبة أمل قوية. devastated وdistraught وinconsolable = حزن شديد جدًا.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Down" and "blue" = a little sad. "Miserable" and "gutted" = quite sad or very disappointed. "Devastated", "distraught" and "inconsolable" = extremely sad.

examples.sentence: It's Monday and I'm feeling a bit blue.
She was devastated when she heard the news.

fine_lines.title: Formal vs informal sadness words
words: gutted, blue, sick as a parrot
fine_lines.explanation_ar: devastated وdistraught وdesolate أكثر رسمية. gutted وblue وas sick as a parrot غير رسمية وتُستخدم في الحديث اليومي.
fine_lines.explanation_en: "Devastated", "distraught" and "desolate" are more formal. "Gutted", "blue" and "as sick as a parrot" are informal, for everyday chat.

examples.sentence: The whole country was devastated by the news.

examples.word: gutted, blue, sick as a parrot
examples.sentence: I'm gutted we lost the match.

expressions.phrase: I just feel a little down.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you are a bit sad without a clear reason.
expressions.example: Nothing's wrong. I just feel a little down today.

expressions.meaning_en: An informal question when someone looks sad.
expressions.example: You're very quiet. What's up with you?
I always feel blue after the holidays.

expressions.phrase: What are you looking so miserable for?
expressions.meaning_en: Asks why someone looks so unhappy.
expressions.example: It's a sunny day! What are you looking so miserable for?

expressions.phrase: We'll get to the bottom of this.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you will find the real reason for a problem.
expressions.example: Let's talk about it. We'll get to the bottom of this.
He didn't get the job. He's gutted.

expressions.phrase: We were devastated to hear the news.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you were deeply shocked and sad.
expressions.example: We were devastated to hear the news about the accident.

expressions.meaning_en: Nothing could make her feel better.
expressions.example: She lost her grandmother's ring and was inconsolable.

expressions.phrase: I'm at the end of my tether.
expressions.meaning_en: Says you can't take any more.
expressions.example: So much pressure at work! I'm at the end of my tether.

expressions.phrase: He's as sick as a parrot.
expressions.meaning_en: Funny British way to say very disappointed.
expressions.example: His team was relegated. He's as sick as a parrot.

expressions.meaning_en: Says someone will feel better in time.
expressions.example: Leave him for now. He'll get over it.

grammar.title: feel / look + adjective
grammar.explanation_ar: بعد feel وlook (بمعنى يبدو) نستخدم الصفة وليس الظرف: feel miserable وليس feel miserably.
grammar.explanation_en: After "feel" and "look" (= seem) use an adjective, not an adverb: feel miserable, not feel miserably.

grammar.title: Adjective + preposition: devastated by, distraught about/over
grammar.explanation_ar: devastated by / at + الخبر. distraught about / over + الشيء. desolated by + الحدث.
grammar.explanation_en: devastated by / at + news; distraught about / over + something; desolated by + an event.
examples: They were devastated by the news.
She was distraught over the lost cat.
He was desolated by the loss of his friend.

questions.question: "He was gutted when he didn't get the job" means he was:
"Nothing we said could help. He was ___."
"I'm at the end of my tether" means:
questions.explanation_en: It means I can't take any more.

questions.question: Which is INFORMAL and British?
questions.explanation_ar: as sick as a parrot تعبير بريطاني غير رسمي.
questions.explanation_en: "As sick as a parrot" is informal British.

questions.question: We were devastated ___ the news.
questions.explanation_ar: نقول devastated by the news (مفجوع بالخبر).

questions.question: "A desolate island" is:
questions.explanation_en: A desolate place is empty and lonely.
